scope: Manual comparison of all twelve remaining p1410 group-invariant testing interfaces, preserving separate source quantifiers, assumption parts and extended-logarithm limitations.

rows.query: Inspected MulAction and its inherited multiplication law in Algebra/Group/Action/Defs and the set-image construction against D4's componentwise action and left translate.
rows.result: A group action and ordinary images express the individual action, coordinatewise extension and set translate; measurability and continuity are additional properties.
rows.gap: Instantiate the left action on observations and parameters, its coordinatewise sample action and set images, with any later measurable-action assumptions stated separately.

comparisons.D4: For a group G use MulAction G X, act on a finite sample vector by (g acting on x)_i=g acting on x_i, and set gB to the image of B under x↦g acting on x. The same construction applies to the parameter space, without identifying it with the observation space. The action laws give identity and composition and group elements act bijectively, but do not alone make images of measurable sets measurable. Left translation is retained; no right-action reversal or multiplication of data coordinates is introduced. The original x^n versus capital X^n typography remains in its source statement and does not imply a separate stochastic operation.

rows.query: Inspected action laws, set images and Measure.map against the exact two-sided family identity (3).
rows.result: Equivariance of the family under pushforward expresses the model property once measurable inverse actions and probability laws are supplied; it is not invariance of each law separately.
rows.gap: State model equivariance under simultaneous parameter and observation actions and prove its equivalence to the printed measurable-set identity.

comparisons.D6: Preserve P_theta(B)=P_{g theta}(gB) for every g, theta and measurable B. With measurable bijections whose inverses are measurable, this is equivalent to map(x↦g x) P_theta=P_{g theta}; do not reverse the pushforward or leave the parameter fixed. The action constructor alone does not supply the measurable image and inverse conditions. The same property applies separately to the group-indexed null and alternative families and does not identify them with each other. A single P_theta need not be invariant under all g, so a measure-preserving action on one fixed probability law would be too strong.

rows.query: Inspected measurable kernels and their probability-normalization predicate against D8's two group-indexed families and the source reparameterization note.
rows.result: A measurable probability kernel is a possible representation of each group-indexed family, but the bare family notation alone neither asserts kernel measurability nor identifies the null and alternative indices.
rows.gap: Represent the two fixed probability-model families on the sample space with their shared group index and separately required equivariance and measurability properties.

comparisons.D8: The null consists of all P_g and the alternative of all Q_g for g in G, each a law of X^n. The two displayed occurrences of g are bound nuisance indices of two hypothesis sets, not a requirement that a null and alternative use the same realized group element. If g↦P_g(B) and g↦Q_g(B) are measurable, Markov kernels package these families for later mixtures; do not infer that extra property solely from family notation. The source derives this representation from parameter orbits, but later theorems can work with the supplied families without importing the reparameterization proof or extra freeness clauses. The sample-law notation is not itself an instruction to rebuild an iid product.

rows.query: Searched Probability for e-statistic/GROW terminology and inspected nonnegative integration, measurability and predicate-defined sets against D10.
rows.result: Measurable nonnegative real statistics with uniformly bounded null expectations can be represented; no martingale or invariance condition is supplied or required by this fixed-sample definition.
rows.gap: Define the class of finite nonnegative measurable statistics whose nonnegative expectation is at most one under every null group parameter.

comparisons.D10: Let T be real-valued, measurable and pointwise nonnegative, and require for every g that the lintegral of ENNReal.ofReal T under P_g is <=1. The group is nonempty, so this family bound represents the printed supremum bound without a real-supremum fallback for unbounded expectations. Nonnegative integration excludes a statistic with infinite null expectation; plain Bochner integration would incorrectly return zero outside integrability if used without hypotheses. The statistic may be zero and need not be invariant, bounded by one pointwise, or a martingale/e-process. Its bounded null expectations do not automatically make logarithmic expectations finite under alternative laws.

rows.query: Inspected ENNReal.log's zero/top branches, nonnegative integration and IsMaxOn against D11 and the recorded logarithmic-expectation limitations.
rows.result: The extended logarithm retains negative infinity at a zero statistic, and a generic maximizer predicate can express optimization once an extended expected-log objective is well defined.
rows.gap: Define well-posed extended expected log growth and maximize its worst-case alternative value over admissible e-statistics without assuming an optimizer exists.

comparisons.D11: For a feasible e-statistic T take inf_g E_Qg[log T], then maximize this criterion over the entire e-statistic class. Because T may vanish, ENNReal.log(ofReal T) has the intended negative-infinity value there, whereas Real.log 0=0 is not a faithful replacement. An extended expectation needs positive/negative-part integration and conventions excluding undefined infinity-minus-infinity; null expectation control alone need not provide alternative-law log integrability. IsMaxOn can compare a supplied objective in an ordered codomain, but feasibility/membership and existence are separate. Preserve should it exist and distinguish this absolute worst-case criterion from the oracle-subtracted relative criterion; no invariance or martingale restriction is added to the optimizing class.

rows.query: Inspected Measure.bind and its measurable-transition interpretation, with kernel normalization, against D2's prior-integrated model law.
rows.result: Binding a probability prior through a measurable probability-law family gives the mixture measure, with the measurable-set integral formula requiring the usual measurability conditions.
rows.gap: Construct the prior mixture as a measurable probability-kernel integral and verify the printed setwise formula while keeping distinct priors separate.

comparisons.D2: Use prior.bind (fun theta => P_theta) after supplying measurability of the measure-valued family, or the corresponding Markov kernel construction. Its mass on measurable B is the integral of P_theta(B) against the probability prior. The superscript theta, or g in group-indexed applications, binds an integration variable and is neither exponentiation nor a group action on a measure. Theorem 1 permits separate priors for the null and alternative mixtures; no shared prior, Haar measure or mixture of likelihood ratios is inferred. A Haar measure on a noncompact group need not be a probability prior and is not silently substituted. The bare bind constructor has no intended probabilistic interpretation without its measurable-transition requirements.

rows.query: Inspected density measures, absolute continuity and group set images against every requirement of Assumption 1 Part 3 and the source common-support note.
rows.result: Dominated probability families and translated-set measures are representable, but relative left invariance with a multiplier and a common support form extra structure beyond ordinary domination.
rows.gap: Package the invariant dominated families, relatively left-invariant common measure and common-support convention without importing the other assumption parts.

comparisons.D16: Keep both model families equivariant and dominated by one mu, with mu(gB)=chi(g)*mu(B) for every measurable B and g. The multiplier is retained rather than set to one, and relative left invariance must not be replaced by right invariance or probability-measure preservation. An implementation must choose the multiplier's positive finite scalar interpretation and handle extended measure masses consistently. All densities have one common support; absolute continuity with respect to the same mu alone does not assert that property, and the source's support/version convention requires explicit interpretation. Theorem 4 assumes only this part, so Polish/local compactness, freeness and amenability are not added through the dependency graph.

rows.query: Searched group, probability and normed-group modules for amenability; compared scalar probability convergence and right set translates with the exact sequence-based D9 definition.
rows.result: The printed pointwise-in-set and group-element convergence is expressible with probability masses and Tendsto; no equivalence to a stronger uniform or invariant-mean formulation was verified.
rows.gap: Define the source's sequence of almost-right-invariant probability measures with its exact quantifiers and keep claimed alternative amenability formulations separate.

comparisons.D9: Choose one sequence Pi_k of probability measures on G such that, for each fixed measurable B and each fixed g, abs(Pi_k(B)-Pi_k(Bg)) tends to zero as k tends to infinity. Bg is the right translate image h↦h*g, and measurability of these translates must be supplied by the ambient group/measurable structure. H is a dummy random group element, not a second measure or a fixed subgroup. No supremum over B, total-variation convergence, uniformity on compact g sets or net in place of the sequence is printed. Keep the later compact-set/right-Haar characterization as separately recorded context; the bounded search and generic convergence tools do not certify equivalence to that or to any standard invariant-mean definition.

rows.query: Inspected orbit and the complete orbitRel equivalence-relation body against D7's invariance and maximal-invariance clauses.
rows.result: The orbit equivalence relation directly expresses which observations must have identical maximal-invariant values; constructing a measurable representative statistic is additional work.
rows.gap: Specify an orbit-constant statistic that separates distinct orbits and verify any required measurability on the chosen statistic space.

comparisons.D7: Ordinary invariance requires m(gx)=m(x) for all g,x. Maximal invariance further requires m(x)=m(x-prime) iff x lies in orbit G x-prime, exactly the relation used by orbitRel. Thus m factors through the orbit quotient and is injective on quotient classes, but need not be onto an arbitrarily chosen codomain. A quotient relation or an abstract representative choice does not automatically provide a measurable statistic or a convenient standard-Borel quotient. The group-action orientation in x=g*x-prime is retained; symmetry of the orbit relation is a consequence of the group laws. Theorem 1's arbitrary statistic V_n is not required to have this stronger property.

rows.query: Inspected PolishSpace's inherited complete-metrizability/second-countability fields and LocallyCompactSpace's neighborhood field and Hausdorff documentation against the entire D13 sentence.
rows.result: Polishness together with local compactness expresses all the source's listed topological requirements for both spaces; local compactness is not part of the PolishSpace class itself.
rows.gap: Instantiate both PolishSpace and LocallyCompactSpace on G and the sample space, keeping the action and topological-group assumptions separate.

comparisons.D13: For each of G and X^n require PolishSpace and LocallyCompactSpace with its given topology. In a metrizable space second countability corresponds to the separability in the source description, and complete metrizability means existence of a compatible complete metric rather than completeness of every chosen metric. Polish spaces are Hausdorff, so the library's compact-neighborhood-basis definition matches the usual local-compactness condition here. Retain the extra local-compactness requirement instead of treating the source dash as a redefinition of Polish. These typeclasses say nothing by themselves about action continuity, group inversion continuity or measure domination, which remain separate clauses.

rows.query: Inspected extended logarithms, nonnegative integration and maximizer predicates against D12's nested alternative-specific oracle subtraction and the registered optimizer-equivalence note.
rows.result: Nested optimization can be specified once log expectations and subtraction are well defined; the relative and absolute criteria are not identical by construction.
rows.gap: Define the oracle-subtracted expected-log objective with its exact optimization order and extended-value conventions, then establish equivalence to GROW only under the theorem's hypotheses.

comparisons.D12: For each fixed g first compute E_Qg[log T]-sup_{T-prime an e-statistic} E_Qg[log T-prime], then take inf over g, and maximize the resulting value over feasible T. The oracle may optimize separately for each g, but each candidate T-prime must still satisfy the full composite-null e-statistic constraint. Do not move the subtraction outside the infimum or use a common oracle optimizer without proof. Zero statistics require the extended logarithm and infinite oracle values can produce undefined differences unless additional conditions resolve them. Theorem 4 proves a constant oracle value and equivalence of optimizer sets under its assumptions; that result is neither this definition nor a proof of optimizer existence, and it does not import the other parts of Assumption 1.

rows.query: Inspected isCancelSMul_iff_eq_one_of_smul_eq, its full proof and Group section parameters, and the IsCancelSMul definition against D5.
rows.result: The theorem's right-hand side is precisely the source's condition that g*z=z forces g to be the identity, giving a direct equivalence with the library free-action predicate.
rows.gap: Instantiate the existing equivalence for the supplied group action; no additional freeness predicate is needed.

comparisons.D5: With Group G and MulAction G Z, isCancelSMul_iff_eq_one_of_smul_eq states IsCancelSMul G Z iff forall g,z, g acting on z=z implies g=1, exactly the printed trivial-stabilizer criterion. Group actions already cancel in the acted-on coordinate, so the library's cancellative-action packaging does not strengthen this source property under the stated group laws. Freeness is distinct from faithfulness, transitivity and invariance of probability models. The condition is vacuous on an empty acted-on set, as is the source formula; no nonemptiness is inserted. Its uses in reparameterization or other assumption parts do not make it a prerequisite of Theorem 4's Part-3-only statement.
